title: Exact Duplicate Removal
description: Exact duplicates are found by hashing full rows and keeping one copy per hash. The hash makes comparison O(n). Deduplication is the first and cheapest quality win.

title: Fuzzy Duplicate Matching
description: Near-duplicates with typos or formatting differences are found by similarity: edit distance, phonetic codes, or embeddings. Blocking limits comparisons to likely pairs. Fuzzy matching catches what exact hashing misses.

title: Mean/Median Imputation
description: Missing numeric values are filled with the column's mean or median. Median resists outliers better. Imputation is honest only when the missingness is documented.

demo.code:
vals = [10, 20, None, 40]
med = sorted(v for v in vals if v is not None)[1]
filled = [med if v is None else v for v in vals]
print("filled:", filled)

title: KNN Imputation
description: Each missing value is filled from its k nearest complete neighbors, preserving local structure better than global means. Distance is computed on the observed features. KNN imputation respects the data's neighborhoods.

demo.code:
pts = [(1, 2), (2, 3), (10, None)]
known = [(x, y) for x, y in pts if y is not None]
mx = sum(x for x, y in known) / len(known)
print("neighbors:", known)
print("imputed y for x=10:", round(sum(y for _, y in known) / len(known), 1))

title: Outlier Detection (IQR)
description: Values beyond 1.5 IQR from the quartiles are flagged as outliers. The rule is simple and robust. Flagged values are investigated, not auto-deleted.

demo.code:
vals = sorted([10, 12, 11, 13, 12, 100])
q1, q3 = vals[1], vals[4]
iqr = q3 - q1
fence = q3 + 1.5 * iqr
print("fence:", fence, "outliers:", [v for v in vals if v > fence])

title: Outlier Repair via Winsorization
description: Extreme values are capped at a percentile instead of removed, preserving the row while taming the tail. Winsorization keeps sample size intact. The distribution's shape survives.

demo.code:
vals = [10, 12, 11, 13, 200]
cap = 15
fixed = [min(v, cap) for v in vals]
print("before:", vals)
print("after: ", fixed)

title: Referential Integrity Repair
description: Foreign keys pointing nowhere are repaired by matching to the closest valid key or nulling with a flag. The repair log records every change. Integrity is restored with an audit trail.

title: Schema Validation Rules
description: Each column gets validation rules: types, ranges, formats, uniqueness. Violations are quarantined with reasons. The rules are the data's immune system.

title: Data Profiling
description: Profiling summarizes every column: nulls, distincts, min/max, patterns. The profile is the dataset's medical chart. Repairs start from the profile.

demo.code:
col = [10, 20, None, 20, 30]
print("nulls:", col.count(None), "distinct:", len(set(v for v in col if v is not None)))
print("min:", min(v for v in col if v is not None), "max:", max(v for v in col if v is not None))
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Profiling', 'defect': 'Unknown quality', 'method': 'Column statistics', 'guarantee': 'Full visibility', 'benefit': 'Medical chart', 'complexity': 'Low'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'defect', 'method', 'guarantee', 'benefit', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Pattern-Based Format Repair
description: Values not matching the expected pattern (phone, date, zip) are repaired by format-specific rules or flagged. Patterns are learned from the valid majority. Format chaos becomes order.

demo.code:
phones = ["555-1234", "5551234", "bad"]
fixed = [p if "-" in p else (p[:3] + "-" + p[3:] if p.isdigit() else "FLAG:" + p) for p in phones]
print(fixed)
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Format repair', 'defect': 'Bad formats', 'method': 'Pattern rules', 'guarantee': 'Conforming formats', 'benefit': 'Order from chaos', 'complexity': 'Medium'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'defect', 'method', 'guarantee', 'benefit', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Cross-Field Consistency Rules
description: Rules spanning columns catch impossible combos: end before start, negative age with veteran status. The rules encode domain knowledge. Inconsistencies are logic errors made visible.

title: Deduplication with Survivorship
description: When duplicates merge, survivorship rules pick the best value per field: newest timestamp, most complete, trusted source. Merging beats deleting because information is preserved. The rules decide what survives.

demo.code:
dupes = [{"name": "Jon", "ts": 1}, {"name": "John", "ts": 2}]
winner = max(dupes, key=lambda d: d["ts"])
print("survivor:", winner)
_jah_schema = {'technique': 'Survivorship', 'defect': 'Conflicting dupes', 'method': 'Per-field rules', 'guarantee': 'Best values kept', 'benefit': 'Information preserved', 'complexity': 'Medium'}
print("technique:", _jah_schema["technique"])
assert set(_jah_schema) == set(['technique', 'defect', 'method', 'guarantee', 'benefit', 'complexity']) and all(_jah_schema.values())
print("schema verified:", len(_jah_schema), "fields")

title: Time-Series Gap Filling

title: Entity Resolution
description: Records referring to the same real-world entity are linked across datasets: same person, different spellings. Blocking plus scoring makes it scale. Resolution unifies fragmented data.
